definition: The size and growth of the market the company sells into.
includes: Addressable market and TAM; industry growth; end-market demand; new markets; adoption.
search_terms: addressable market; TAM; industry growth; end-market demand; new market; adoption

definition: The company's share of its market: customers won or lost against rivals.
includes: Market share; customer wins and contract awards; churn; new entrants; competitor exits.
search_terms: market share; customer wins; contract award; churn; new entrant; competitor exit

definition: Revenue and volume, where the article doesn't say whether the change comes from the market or from share.
includes: Revenue and sales; shipments; orders, bookings and backlog; same-store sales; subscribers.
route_elsewhere: Growth attributed to the market -> TAM; to winning or losing customers -> SHARE.
search_terms: revenue; sales; shipments; orders; bookings; backlog; same-store sales; subscribers

definition: The company's ability to set its prices: raising, cutting or holding them, and passing costs on.
includes: Price increases and cuts; discounting; cost pass-through; pricing pressure.
route_elsewhere: Costs and tariffs on what the company buys -> COST.
search_terms: price increase; price cut; discounting; pass-through; pricing pressure

definition: The company's costs and efficiency, which set its margins together with pricing.
includes: Restructuring and layoffs; cost savings; automation; input costs; wage inflation; tariffs; operating margin.
search_terms: restructuring; layoffs; cost savings; automation; input costs; wage inflation; tariffs; operating margin

definition: How much the company must invest to deliver its growth.
includes: Capex; new plants and capacity expansion; inventory, receivables and working capital; acquisitions; R&D; asset-light models.
search_terms: capex; new plant; capacity expansion; inventory; receivables; working capital; acquisition; R&D; asset-light

definition: The return equity investors demand of the company: rates and the risk premium they apply.
includes: Interest rates and Treasury yields; risk premium; country risk; sovereign rating.
search_terms: interest rates; Treasury yields; risk premium; country risk; sovereign rating

definition: The company's cost of borrowing, net of tax advantages.
includes: Credit rating and downgrades; refinancing; notes offerings; spreads; credit facilities; interest expense.
search_terms: credit rating; downgrade; refinancing; notes offering; spread; credit facility; interest expense

topic: Catastrophic event threatening the business model
definition: The chance of a grievous or catastrophic event that puts the business model at risk.
includes: Going-concern doubts; Chapter 11 and default; covenant breach; liquidity; fraud and restatements; a revoked license; nationalization; an FDA rejection.
search_terms: going concern; Chapter 11; default; covenant breach; liquidity; fraud; restatement; license revoked; nationalization; FDA rejection

definition: The company's share price, the market's reaction, its valuation, or an analyst's rating or price target.
includes: Share-price moves; market value; valuation multiples; analyst ratings, price targets and estimates.
route_elsewhere: A statement that also explains the business (results, prices, costs, guidance) -> tag the driver it states as well.

definition: The unit comes from promotional or stock-picking content rather than reporting or analysis of the company: a list of stocks to buy, a ranking, a newsletter or 'read next' plug.
includes: '10 best AI stocks to buy', 'billionaires' favourite picks', 'is X the best stock to buy now?'.

definition: Content about the company that does not clearly fit any topic in this codebook.
